what_this_is: First on-chain deployments of the ZK predicate contract and the many-agreement registry. Both had passed their local simulators; this is the first time either produced a real zero-knowledge proof.

predicates.what_is_public: the label, the comparison, the threshold, a commitment to the measurement, and the result
predicates.what_is_not: the measurement itself, which never left the prover

registry.reuse_refused_on_chain: Unexpected error executing scoped transaction '<unnamed>': Error: failed assert: an agreement with this manifest hash already exists
registry.what_this_shows: Two agreements settled inside ONE deployment, and a third attempt to reuse an existing manifest hash was refused by the circuit. The previous design needed one deployment per agreement.

multisig.what_this_shows: Two distinct finalizers approved in separate transactions and only then could the escrow settle. One key holder cannot settle alone on this rail — which the other three rails still permit.

caveat: Testnet. tNIGHT has no value. Local simulation proves circuit logic; this proves proofs verify on a real chain. Neither proves the contracts are free of defects — see docs/THREAT-MODEL.md.
